input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now shares and clears a single statistics dict on every call. Every call of the wrapped function, including concurrent or nested ones, reuses and clears the same dict object. The previous code gave each call its own copy's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function runs concurrently in threads or asyncio tasks, or recursively. Mechanism: stats.clear() wipes the dict that an in-flight call is still updating, and both calls write into the same dict through copy._local.statistics. Impact: attempt_number, delay_since_first_attempt and idle_for become corrupted or mixed between calls, and the mixing can also make retry decisions wrong.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. A single statistics dict is shared and cleared on every call, so concurrent or nested calls clear and overwrite each other's statistics and leave them corrupted. The trigger and impact also match.
